# Security boundaries

Where untrusted input enters Ono-Sendai, what must hold before it goes further, the one crate responsible for making it hold, and the automated negative test that proves the forbidden thing is refused (v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §20). Derived from `docs/spec/hardening/security_boundaries.yaml`, which the contract gate reads as well: a boundary whose owner changes cannot leave this page saying otherwise.

| Boundary | Input trust | Required enforcement | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `remote.tcp.transport` | network | TLS 1.3 + mutual peer proof | `ono-remote` |
| `remote.tcp.authorization` | authenticated peer | explicit server policy | `ono-protocol` |
| `remote.ssh.transport` | ssh channel | external SSH authentication | `ono-remote` |
| `protocol.frame` | peer bytes | size/depth/version limits | `ono-protocol` |
| `provider.query` | authorized request | provider capability contract | `ono-protocol` |
| `provider.act` | authorized request | capability + risk/elevation checks | `ono-protocol` |
| `kuang.native.spawn` | package process | manifest + fail-closed confinement | `ono-kuang-supervisor` |
| `kuang.protocol` | plugin bytes | frame/credit/schema limits | `ono-kuang-protocol` |
| `external.adapter` | process output | adapter decoder and schema validation | `ono-adapter` |
| `pipeline.materialization` | value stream | count + byte budget | `ono-value` |
| `release.build` | CI inputs | immutable refs + locked dependencies | `xtask` |
| `release.publish` | artifacts | checksum + signature + provenance | `xtask` |

## `remote.tcp.transport`

§6.2's own example: "TLS peer proof belongs in `ono-remote`, not in CLI rendering." The listener requires a client certificate and verifies possession of the key before a single Ono byte is read (§13.1), so an unauthenticated peer never reaches the protocol at all. The client half of the same boundary — the pinned host key — is enforced in `crates/ono-remote/src/tls.rs` and refuses a changed key rather than asking about it (§2.9).

Owned by `ono-remote`, enforced in `crates/ono-remote/src/listener.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §7.1, §7.4, §13.1, §13.4.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-remote/tests/client_authentication.rs::should_refuse_a_tls_client_that_presents_no_certificate`
- `crates/ono-remote/tests/client_authentication.rs::should_refuse_a_tls_client_that_cannot_prove_it_holds_the_key_it_presents`
- `crates/ono-remote/tests/client_authentication.rs::should_refuse_a_tls_client_that_asks_for_another_application_protocol`
- `crates/ono-remote/tests/trust.rs::should_refuse_a_changed_host_key_with_the_stable_safety_code`

## `remote.tcp.authorization`

§9.1: authentication proves possession of a key and does not prove the operator wants that key to see the system. The `AuthorizationContext` is built from the authenticated fingerprint at accept and is immutable for the life of the connection (§10.3), so nothing the peer says about itself reaches the decision (§65.2). A store that will not parse fails closed rather than reading as an empty policy (§59.5).

Owned by `ono-protocol`, enforced in `crates/ono-protocol/src/authorization.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §9.1, §9.4, §10.3, §59.5.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_refuse_an_unlisted_client_before_provider_negotiation`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_disclose_no_process_schema_or_capability_inventory_to_an_unlisted_client`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_refuse_a_client_the_transport_authenticated_as_nobody`
- `crates/ono-cli/tests/authorized_clients.rs::should_never_treat_a_malformed_store_as_an_empty_one`

## `remote.ssh.transport`

The one boundary Ono does not enforce itself, which is why it is in the inventory: the SSH carrier decided who may run the command, and the shell's obligation is to say so rather than to imply a proof it does not have. `get link` reports no proved key over a transport that proves nothing (§51.3), and a policy-governed grant is not consulted here because there is no fingerprint to key one on.

Owned by `ono-remote`, enforced in `crates/ono-remote/src/transport.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §4.3, §51.3.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-remote/tests/trust.rs::should_refuse_an_unauthenticated_transport_when_trust_is_required`
- `crates/ono-cli/tests/authenticated_link.rs::should_report_no_proved_key_over_a_transport_that_proves_nothing`
- `crates/ono-remote/tests/agentless.rs::should_refuse_to_open_an_agentless_link_to_a_far_side_that_does_not_answer`

## `protocol.frame`

§6.2's second example: "wire size limits belong in `ono-protocol`, not in command handlers." A declared length larger than the ceiling is refused *before* the allocation it declares, which is the difference between a refusal and the memory exhaustion it would otherwise cause. The ceilings themselves are `limits.remote_*` in `docs/spec/hardening/limits.yaml`, so no number is typed here (§52.2).

Owned by `ono-protocol`, enforced in `crates/ono-protocol/src/frame.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §13.2, §56.2.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/framing.rs::should_refuse_a_frame_claiming_more_than_the_limit_before_allocating`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/framing.rs::should_refuse_a_frame_whose_version_is_not_the_one_we_speak`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/framing.rs::should_refuse_a_frame_whose_kind_is_not_in_the_protocol`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/framing.rs::should_refuse_a_frame_whose_reserved_bits_are_set`

## `provider.query`

§10.1 filters the offer and §10.2 says that is not the enforcement: "negotiation filtering is not sufficient by itself." Both dispatch sites ask the same immutable context — the protocol loop before it hands the request on, and the service before it touches the registry — so a request that reaches a provider unchecked needs two independent pieces of code to be wrong at once (ADR-0472).

Owned by `ono-protocol`, enforced in `crates/ono-protocol/src/service.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §10.1, §10.2, §20, §65.3.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_refuse_a_request_for_a_capability_the_offer_omitted`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_refuse_it_on_every_dispatch_path_the_server_exposes`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_offer_only_the_capabilities_the_clients_policy_allows`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_leave_an_ungranted_action_capability_out_of_the_offer_the_provider_advertises`

## `provider.act`

The capability an action needs is resolved by the serving side from this agent's own command contracts, never read from the request, because a peer that names the capability it needs is authorizing itself (§65.2). An id this side cannot name is denied, which is Appendix C's rule and also covers a capability a later version introduces. `adapt` runs a program of the caller's choosing and no entry in `docs/spec/capabilities.yaml` names it, so no grant can name it and every policy-governed connection is refused it.

Owned by `ono-protocol`, enforced in `crates/ono-protocol/src/service.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §9.5, §9.6, §10.2, Appendix C.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_deny_an_action_whose_capability_id_is_unknown`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_deny_a_capability_introduced_after_the_grant_was_written`
- `crates/ono-protocol/tests/authorization.rs::should_leave_every_ungranted_action_refused_when_one_action_is_granted`
- `crates/ono-cli/tests/authorized_clients.rs::should_refuse_a_wildcard_or_risk_class_in_an_action_grant`

## `kuang.native.spawn`

§6.2's third example: "native process setup errors belong in `ono-kuang-supervisor`/process code, not in a later audit view." Every mandatory control is installed between fork and exec and its return value is checked (§16.2), so a control that could not be installed stops the exec rather than being noticed afterwards. Which controls are mandatory is `docs/spec/hardening/kuang_confinement_controls.yaml`, once (§52.2).

Owned by `ono-kuang-supervisor`, enforced in `crates/ono-kuang-supervisor/src/sandbox.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §16.1, §16.2, §16.3, §18.1, Appendix D.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-kuang-supervisor/tests/confinement.rs::should_never_exec_the_plugin_when_a_mandatory_control_cannot_be_installed`
- `crates/ono-kuang-supervisor/tests/confinement.rs::should_leave_the_plugins_startup_marker_absent_after_a_failed_confinement_setup`
- `crates/ono-kuang-supervisor/tests/confinement.rs::should_never_hand_back_a_plugin_whose_report_is_not_confined`
- `crates/ono-kuang-supervisor/tests/confinement.rs::should_check_the_result_of_every_control_the_table_marks_mandatory`

## `kuang.protocol`

A loaded plugin is a separate process speaking a framed protocol, and its bytes are as untrusted as a network peer's: the host is what a hostile package attacks. The manifest is parsed fail-closed — an unknown key in a closed section is a refusal rather than an ignored field — and a nested document is refused before the nesting costs anything.

Owned by `ono-kuang-protocol`, enforced in `crates/ono-kuang-protocol/src/frame.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §18.2, §18.3.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-kuang-protocol/src/frame.rs::should_refuse_an_oversized_declaration_before_allocating_when_reading`
- `crates/ono-kuang-protocol/src/frame.rs::should_refuse_garbage_bytes_as_malformed_when_decoding`
- `crates/ono-kuang-protocol/tests/manifest_validation.rs::should_refuse_a_nested_document_before_it_costs_anything_to_refuse_it`
- `crates/ono-kuang-protocol/tests/manifest_validation.rs::should_refuse_an_unknown_capability_id_rather_than_ignore_it`

## `external.adapter`

The output of a program the shell did not write, decoded into objects the shell promises a schema for. Truncated output fails structurally and keeps the bytes rather than yielding a half-record that looks like data, and a field of the wrong type is a schema violation rather than a coerced value — spec §35.3's "unknown is null, never fabricated" applied to the one input the product cannot constrain.

Owned by `ono-adapter`, enforced in `crates/ono-adapter/src/decode.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §50; v0.3 §1.54.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-adapter/tests/decode.rs::should_report_a_schema_violation_when_a_field_has_the_wrong_type`
- `crates/ono-adapter/tests/decode.rs::should_fail_structurally_on_truncated_output_and_keep_the_bytes`
- `crates/ono-adapter/tests/decode.rs::should_never_panic_on_hostile_bytes`

## `pipeline.materialization`

§6.2's fourth example: "byte-budget enforcement belongs in the materialization primitive, not in each caller independently." One `Budget` type carries both ceilings, has no constructor that leaves either unset (§65.6 names a count-only limit as a failure mode), and refuses rather than truncating — a silently shortened answer is §2.6's unknown pretending to be a result.

Owned by `ono-value`, enforced in `crates/ono-value/src/budget.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §21.1, §21.3, §22.2, §65.6.

Refusal proved by:

- `crates/ono-pipeline/tests/budget.rs::should_refuse_rather_than_truncate_when_a_budget_is_exceeded`
- `crates/ono-pipeline/tests/budget.rs::should_offer_no_default_that_leaves_a_budget_unlimited`
- `crates/ono-pipeline/tests/budget.rs::should_require_both_an_item_and_a_byte_ceiling_when_a_budget_is_constructed`
- `crates/ono-pipeline/tests/budget.rs::should_charge_a_nested_budget_against_the_budget_it_was_taken_from`

## `release.build`

The inputs a release trusts are a boundary in the same sense a socket is: everything that runs during a build can write to the artifact. §43.2 asks that critical logic live in first-party code rather than in a third-party action, so the owner is this repository's own `xtask` and the scanners run on every gate, not only on a tag. §65.11 names a mutable release input as a failure mode outright.

Owned by `xtask`, enforced in `xtask/src/supply_chain.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §43.1, §43.2, §44.1, §44.4, §65.11.

Refusal proved by:

- `xtask/tests/supply_chain.rs::should_reject_an_action_referenced_by_a_floating_tag`
- `xtask/tests/supply_chain.rs::should_reject_a_build_image_pulled_by_tag_alone`
- `xtask/tests/supply_chain.rs::should_reject_a_workflow_that_grants_write_access_to_every_job`
- `xtask/tests/supply_chain.rs::should_reject_a_publishing_job_a_pull_request_can_reach`

## `release.publish`

§49.1's "build once, promote after proof": the bytes that were tested are the bytes that ship, and what makes that checkable from outside is the checksum manifest, the signature over it and the provenance binding each digest to the inputs of Appendix H. A real signature needs an OIDC token that exists only inside a release run, so the end-to-end proof is owed by the first `v*` tag and `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md` §4.8.11 says so in the box.

Owned by `xtask`, enforced in `xtask/src/provenance.rs`. Specified by v0.4.1 §6.1, §6.2, §47.2, §47.3, §47.4, §49.1, §62.5.

Refusal proved by:

- `xtask/tests/provenance.rs::should_fail_verification_when_the_checksum_manifest_is_altered`
- `xtask/tests/provenance.rs::should_fail_the_release_check_when_an_artifact_is_absent_from_the_manifest`
- `xtask/tests/provenance.rs::should_verify_every_artifact_digest_against_the_checksum_manifest_and_the_provenance_before_publication`
- `xtask/tests/provenance.rs::should_bind_all_seven_required_fields_to_every_artifact_digest`
